tei:titleStmt.tei:title: תפילה לתענית
The Six Additional Blessings for a 24-Blessing ‘Amidah for Declared Fast Days, according to Vat. Ross. 499 fol. 57v–62r (1446)

tei:div.tei:head: The Six Additional Blessings for a 24-Blessing ‘Amidah for Declared Fast Days, according to Vat. Ross. 499 fol. 57v–62r (1446)

tei:l.tei:note: This is the prayer for fast days
that the great sages compiled
from the words of the rabbis for a blessing and from the Talmud,
and it is good for any time of stress,
may it not come upon the community,
Prayer for a Fast Day
When the prayer-leader reaches “Merciful One, who increases forgiveness,”
say seliḥot and petitions, increasing according to time and according to one’s own knowledge.
The rule is to do it like other fast days, like the order written in this cycle.
And when reaching “Redeemer of Israel” lengthen therein,
and say it up to “And redeem us, our Sovereign, quickly, for Your name’s sake,”
and before saying the conclusion say —

tei:lg.tei:l: May the One who answered Abraham our father on Mt. Moriah
answer us
and hear the sound of our shouts
and redeem us from all stresses!

tei:l.tei:note: And continue:

tei:lg.tei:l: Our God and God of our ancestors,
remember us with good memory before You,
and recall us with a recollection of salvation and compassion
from the highest heavens of old,
and remember for us, Cause our God,
the covenant and mercy and oath
that You swore to Abraham our father on Mt. Moriah,
and let the binding be visible before You,
that Abraham our father bound his son Isaac
on the back of the altar, as written:
And Isaac said to Abraham his father, quote: “Dad?”
And he said, “I’m here, son.”
And he said, “Here’s the kindling and the wood,
but where’s the lamb for the offering?”
And Abraham said:
“God will see to the lamb for the offering – my son.”
And the two of them walked together. (Genesis 22:7–8)
And they came to the place that God had told him,
and there Abraham built an altar
and arranged the wood
and bound Isaac his son
and set him on the altar above the wood.
And Abraham stretched his hand
and took up the cleaver to slaughter his son. (Genesis 22:9–10)
And a messenger of the Cause called to him from heaven and said,
“Abraham! Abraham!”
And he said: “I’m here!”
And he said: “Don’t raise your hand against the lad,
nor do anything to him,
for now I know that you are a God-fearer,
and did not withhold your son, your only one, from Me.” (Genesis 22:11–12)
And Abraham raised his eyes and saw:
hey, a ram, back there, caught in the brush by its horns.
And Abraham went and took the ram
and offered it up as an offering instead of his son.
And Abraham called that place by the name “The Cause will see,”
where today it is said, on the mountain of the Cause is vision. (Genesis 22:13–14)
Thus may Your compassion overpower Your anger
and Your compassion roll over Your attributes,
and be led with Your children with the attribute of mercy,
and enter them as beyond the letter of the law.
And in Your great goodness
turn back Your raging anger
from Your city
and from Your land
and from Your inheritance
and from Your people Israel.
Our God and God of our ancestors,
end from us famine,
plague and pestilence,
blight and rot,
locust and grasshopper,
all injury and all sickness,
and bring down on us rains of desire, blessing, and gift.
And respond: Amen.

tei:l.tei:note: And the community raises one or two people,
experts in horn-blowing, sin-fearing,
either of the seed of Aaron or the seed of holy people.
And the sexton of the community,
that is the beadle of the community, says,
“Blow, children of Aaron, blow!”
or “Blast, children of Aaron, blast!” if they are priests blowing.
If they are non-priests, they say “Blow, children of the holy, blow!” —
or “Blast!” depending of what they are blasting.
The first time, they blast:

tei:lg.tei:l: t’qiah, sh’varim, t’ruah, t’qiah.

tei:l.tei:note: And the prayer-leader says:

tei:lg.tei:l: May the One who answered Abraham our father on Mt. Moriah
answer us and hear the sound of our shouts
and redeem us from all stresses on this day,
for a strong Redeemer are You.
Blessed are You, Cause, Redeemer of Israel.
And respond: Amen.

tei:l.tei:note: If it is a drought, read from Kings:

tei:lg.tei:l: And when the heavens are closed
and there is no precipitation,
for they sinned against You,
and they pray to this place
and acknowledge Your name,
and return from their sin,
You will answer them.
As for You, hear [in] heaven
and forgive the sin of Your servants and Your people Israel,
for You taught them the good path they should walk,
and give them rain on Your land
that You gave Your people as an inheritance.
If famine is in the land, plague,
if there is blight, rot, locust, grasshoper,
if it is that their enemy is beseiging them in the land of their gates,
all injury and all sickness —
any prayer and any petition that is of any person,
of all Your people Israel
(for each person knows their heart’s injury)
and spreads their palms to this house,
as for You, You will hear [in] heaven, Your enthroned abode,
and forgive, and act, and give
each person according to their ways —
as You know their heart, for as for You,
You alone know the heart of all mortal humans.
That they may revere You all the days
that they live on the face of the land
that You gave our ancestors. (I Kings 8:35–40)

tei:l.tei:note: After this blessing, add six more blessings between “Redeemer” and “Healer,”
and for the first blessing say the verses of remembrance per the order of the New Year,
and begin:

tei:lg.tei:l: You remember the universe’s works,
and account for all creatures of yore.
Before You all secrets are revealed,
and many hidden things since creation.
For there is no forgetting before Your honored throne,
nor is there hiding from before Your eyes.
You remember all acts,
and no creature could be deceiving before You. —

tei:l.tei:note: Skip and continue —

tei:lg.tei:l: Content is the person who does not forget You,
the mortal who takes courage in You.
For all who seek You will never be disgraced,
nor will You ever destroy all who hope in You.
So too, Noaḥ in love You remembered,
accounting for him in an accounting of salvation and compasssion,
when You brought the floodwaters to destroy all
on account of the evil of their deeds.
Thus his memory came before You, Cause our God,
to multiply his seed like the dust of the earth
and his descendants like the sand of the sea.
As is written in Your teaching:
And God remembered Noaḥ
and all the wild and tame animals
that were with him in the box,
and God made a wind pass over the earth,
and the water drained. (Genesis 8:1)
And it is written:
And God heard their groans,
and God remembered Their covenant
with Abraham,
with Isaac,
and with Jacob. (Exodus 2:24)
And it is written:
And I will remember My covenant with Jacob,
and also My covenant with Isaac,
and also My covenant with Abraham I will remember,
and the land I will remember. (Leviticus 26:42)
And in Your hagiographia it is written, quote:
A memorial They made for Their wonders;
merciful and compassionate is the Cause.
Food They gave to those revering Them;
They forever remember Their covenant. (Psalms 111:4–5)
And it is written:
They forever remembered Their covenant,
the word They commanded to a thousand ages. (Psalms 105:8)
And it is written:
And They remembered Their covenant for them
and comforted them by Their great mercy. (Psalms 106:45)
And by the hand of Your servants the prophets it is said:
Go and call in the ears of Jerusalem, quote:
Thus says the Cause: I remember you,
your youthful grace, your bridal love,
your going after Me in the wild,
in a land unsown. (Jeremiah 2:2)
And it is written:
And I will remember My covenant with you in your youthful days
and establish with you an eternal covenant. (Ezekiel 16:60)
And it is written:
Isn’t Ephraim a precious son to me, a dandled child?
For whatever I spoke against him, I will remember,
yes, remember him again;
this My innards yearn for him;
I will have compassion, compassion in him —
declares the Cause. (Jeremiah 31:19)
Our God and God of our ancestors,
may our prayers come before You,
and hear the sound of our shouts,
and just as You answered our ancestors at the Reed Sea
answer us, as written:
And you, raise your staff
and stretch your hand over the sea and split it,
and the children of Israel will go into the sea on dry land.
And as for Me, hey, I have strengthened the heart of Egypt,
and they will go after them,
and I will be glorified through Pharaoh and all his force,
through his chariots and horsemen.
And Egypt will know that I am the Cause,
in My glorification through Pharaoh,
through his chariots and horsemen.” (Exodus 14:16–17)
And the angel of God set out going
before the camp of Israel,
and went after them,
and the pillar of cloud set out from before them
and stood behind them.
And it came between the camp of Egypt and the camp of Israel,
and there was the cloud of darkness,
and it illuminated the light,
and they did not come one near another all night. (Exodus 14:18–20)
And Moses lifted his hand over the sea,
and the Cause corralled the sea with a strong east wind all night,
and made the sea into dry land and the waters were split.
And the children of Israel went into the sea,
and the water was a wall for them
on their left and on their right. (Exodus 14:21–22)
And Egypt chased and came after them,
every horse of Pharaoh, his chariot and horsemen,
into the midst of the sea.
And it was the morning watch,
and the Cause looked out upon the camp of Egypt
in a pillar of fire and cloud,
and panicked the camp of Egypt.
And They locked their chariots’ wheels
and they moved with difficulty,
and Egypt said, “Let me flee from Israel,
for the Cause is fighting for them against Egypt.” (Exodus 14:23–25)
And the Cause said to Moses,
“Lift your hand over the sea,
and the water will return over Egypt,
over its chariots and horsemen.”
And Moses lifted his hand over the sea,
and the sea returned that morning to its strength,
and Egypt was fleeing towards it,
and the Cause overturned Egypt in the midst of the sea.
And the waters returned
and covered the chariot and the horsemen,
all the force of Pharaoh which came after them into the sea;
not even one of them remained. (Exodus 14:26–28)
And the children of Israel had walked on dry ground
in the midst of the sea,
and the water was a wall for them
on their left and on their right.
And the Cause saved Israel on that day
from the hand of Egypt,
and Israel saw Egypt dead on the seashore.
And Israel saw the great hand
which the Cause did against Egypt,
and the people were in awe of the Cause,
and believed in the Cause
and in Moses Their servant. (Exodus 14:29–31)

tei:l.tei:note: And they blast:

tei:lg.tei:l: t’qiah, sh’varim, t’qiah,

tei:l.tei:note: and after that say:

tei:lg.tei:l: May the One who answered our ancestors at the Reed Sea
answer us and not forget us on this day,
for a Rememberer of the forgotten are You.
Blessed are You, Cause, Rememberer of the forgotten.
And respond: Amen.

tei:l.tei:note: And for the second blessing say the verses of the shofar.

tei:lg.tei:l: You were revealed in Your glorious cloud
upon Your holy people to speak with them.
From heaven You made Your voice heard
and were revealed upon them in cumuli of purity.
And so too all the world shakes before You,
and created creatures quakes at You.
In Your revealing Yourself, o Sovereign, upon Mt. Sinai,
to teach Your people teaching and commandments,
You made them hear the glory of Your voice
and words of Your holiness from flames of fire.
In thunder and lightning You were revealed upon them,
and in the sound of the shofar You were shown upon them.
As is written in Your teaching:
And it was on the third day, in the morning,
and thunder and lighting and a heavy cloud upon the mountain,
and the sound of the shofar was very strong,
and all the people who were in the camp quaked. (Exodus 19:16)
And it is written:
And the sound of the shofar crescendoed greatly;
Moses would speak and God responded aloud. (Exodus 19:19)
And it is written:
And all the people saw
the sounds and the flames
and the sound of the shofar
and the mountain smoking,
and the people saw and fled
and stood from afar. (Exodus 20:14)
And in Your hagiographia it is written, quote:
God rises with blasting,
the Cause with the shofar’s sound. (Psalms 47:6)
And it is written:
With trumpets and the sound of the shofar,
raise a shout before the Sovereign Cause. (Psalms 98:6)
And it is written:
Praise Yah!
Praise the Deity in Their holiness,
praise Them in the firmament of Their strength.
Praise Them by Their mighty acts,
praise Them by Their great goodness.
Praise Them with blowing the shofar,
praise Them with lyre and harp.
Praise Them with drum and dance,
praise Them with pipe and flute.
Praise Them with sounding cymbals,
praise Them with blasting cymbals.
Let all with breath praise Yah,
praise Yah! (Psalms 150:1-6)
And by the hand of Your servants the prophets it is said:
All the land’s inhabitants and earth’s residents,
at the lifting and raising of the flag, see it;
and at the blowing of the shofar is blown, hear it. (Isaiah 18:3)
And it is written:
And on that day the great shofar will be blown,
and all those lost in the land of Assyria
and exiled in the land of Egypt
will bow before the Cause at the holy mountain in Jerusalem. (Isaiah 27:13)
And it is written:
And the Cause will be seen upon them,
and Their arrows will go out like lightning,
and the Cause, Master, with a shofar blowing,
will go in the southern storms.
The Cause of Forces will guard them. (Zechariah 9:14–15)
The Cause of Forces will guard you.
The Cause of Forces will guard us,
and all Your people Israel in Your peace.
If our iniquities testify against us, Cause,
act per Your name,
though our strayings are great;
we have sinned before You.
Hope of Israel, its Savior in a time of stress!
Why would You be like a stranger in the land,
or like a wayfarer turning aside for a night?
Why would You be like a terrified man,
like a hero who cannot save?
You in our midst are the Cause,
and Your name is called over us;
do not leave us be! (Jeremiah 14:7–9)
Our God and God of our ancestors,
blow the great shofar for our freedom,
and raise a flag to gather our exiles,
and bring together our scattered from among the nations,
and bring in and our exiled from the ends of the earth,
and hear the sound of our shouts and our blasting,
and just as You answered Joshua in Gilgal
answer us, as written:
And when Joshua was in Jericho he raised his eyes and saw,
hey, a man standing before him, his sword drawn in his hand!
And Joshua went to him and said to him,
“Are you one of ours’ or our foes?”
And he said, “No, I am the general of the force of the Cause.
Now I have come.”
And Joshua bowed on his face earthwards and prostrated,
and said to him, “What does milord say to his servant?”
And the general of the force of the Cause said to Joshua:​
“Remove your sandal from your feet,
for the place where you are standing is holy ground,”
and Joshua did so. (Joshua 5:13–5:15)
And Jericho was closed in and closed off
on account of the Israelites;
none could get out and none could get in.
And the Cause said to Joshua,​
“See, I have given Jericho in your hand,
and its king, its mighty warriors.
And go around the city, all the people of war,
and orbit the city one time,
do thus six days.
And seven priests will carry seven ram’s horn shofars before the ark,
and on the seventh day you will go around the city seven times,
and the priests will blow the shofars.
And upon lengthening the ram’s horn blowing,
as you hear the sound of the shofar,
all the people will raise a great blast,
and the city wall will collapse under it,
and the people will go up, each forward.” (Joshua 6:1–6:5)
And Joshua son of Nun called to the priests and said to them,
“Take the ark of the covenant,
and seven priests should carry seven ram’s horn shofars
before the ark of the Cause.”
And he said to the people,
“Pass and encircle the city,
and the vanguard going in front of the ark of the Cause.” (Joshua 6:6–6:7)
And as Joshua had said to the people,
the seven priests carrying seven ram’s horn shofars
went before the Cause,
passing and blowing the shofars.
And the ark of the covenant of the Cause was going after them
and the vanguard going in front of the priests
blowing the shofarot,
and the rearguard was going behind the ark,
going and blowing the shofarot
And the people Joshua commanded, quote:
“Don’t raise a blast,
don’t make a noise heard,
not a word from your mouths,
until the day I say to you to raise a blast,
then you will raise a blast.” (Joshua 6:8–6:10)
And the ark of the Cause went around
and orbited the city one time,
and they went to the camp and stayed in the camp.
And Joshua woke up early in the morning
and the priests took up the ark of the Cause.
And seven priests carrying seven ram’s horn shofars
before the ark of the Cause were going,
going and blasting on the shofars,
and the vanguard going before them,
and the rearguard after the ark of the Cause,
going and blasting with shofars.
And they encircled the city on the second day one time,
and returned to the camp;
thus they did six days. (Joshua 6:11–6:14)
And it was on the seventh day,
and they got up early at sunrise
and encircled the city per the rule:
seven times specifically on that day,
they encircled the city seven times. (Joshua 6:15)
And on the seventh time the priests blew on the shofars,
and Joshua said to the people,
“Raise a blast, because the Cause has given you the city!
And the city is to be condemned,
it and all that is in it is the Cause’s.
Only Raḥaḇ the whore will live,
and those that are with her in her house,
for she hid the messengers who we sent.
And you certainly must keep this condemnation,
lest you be condemned!
And if you take from what is condemned
you will make the camp of Israel condemnation,
and disturb it.
And all silver and gold and bronze and iron tools
are holy to the Cause;
they will go to the Cause’s treasury.” (Joshua 6:16–6:19)
And the people raised a blast and blew the shofars,
and when the people heard the shofars blown
they raised a great blast,
and the walls fell under it,
and the people went up unto the city,
each straight ahead,
and captured the city. (Joshua 6:20)

tei:l.tei:note: And they blast:

tei:lg.tei:l: t’qiah, t’ruah, t’qiah.

tei:l.tei:note: and after that say:

tei:lg.tei:l: May the One who answered Joshua at Gilgal
answer us
and hear the sound of our shouts
and our blasting on this day,
for a Deity who hears blasts are You.
Blessed are You, Cause, who hears blasts.
And respond: Amen.
To the Cause in the strife I faced,
I called and They answered.
Cause, redeem my being from lying lips,
from a slippery tongue!
What can you get,
what can you gain,
o slippery tongue?
Warrior’s arrows, sharpened,
hot coals of bramble.
Woe is me, for I dwell in Meshekh,
that I live with the nomads’ tents!
So long I myself have lived here,
with those who hate peace.
I am “Peace!” but as I speak,
they are for war. (Psalms 120:2-7)
Our God and God of our ancestors,
hear the sound of our shouts,
and just as You answered Samuel in Miẓpah
answer us, as written:
And Samuel said,
“Gather all Israel towards Miẓpah,
and I will pray for you to the Cause.”
And they gathered towards Miẓpah,
and drew water and poured it before the Cause,
and fasted on that day, and said there,
“We have sinned against the Cause,”
and Samuel judged the children of Israel at Miẓpah. (I Samuel 7:5-6)
And the Philistines heard
that the children of Israel had gathered towards Miẓpah,
and the Philistine tyrants went up against Israel,
and the children of Israel heard
and were afraid of the Philistines.
And the children of Israel said to Samuel,
“Do not be silent from us,
not crying out to the Cause our God,
who will save us from the hand of the Philistines!” (I Samuel 7:7-8)
And Samuel took one suckling lamb
and offered it up as a whole burnt-offering to the Cause,
and Samuel cried out to the Cause for Israel’s sake,
and the Cause answered him. (I Samuel 7:9)

tei:l.tei:note: And they blast:

tei:lg.tei:l: t’qiah, sh’varim, t’ruah, t’qiah.

tei:l.tei:note: and after that say:

tei:lg.tei:l: May the One who answered Samuel at Miẓpah
answer us and hear the sound of our shouts on this day,
for a Deity who hears shouts are You.
Blessed are You, Cause, who hears shouts.
And respond: Amen.
I lift my eyes to the mountains;
from where will my help come?
My help will come from the Cause, Maker of heaven and earth.
Your foot They will not let slip,
nor does your Guardian sleep.
Behold, the Guardian of Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps!
The Cause guards you,
the Cause is your shade on your right hand.
By day the sun will not strike you,
nor the moon by night.
The Cause will guard you from all evil,
will guard your life.
The Cause will guard your goings and comings,
from now and forevermore. (Psalms 121:1-8)
Our God and God of our ancestors,
hear the sound of our prayers,
and just as You answered Elijah at Mt. Carmel
answer us, as written:
And at the grain-offering time
Elijah the Prophet drew near and said,
“Cause, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel!
Today let it be known
that You are God in Israel
and I am Your servant
and in Your word I have done all these things!
Answer me, Cause, answer me,
that this people know that You, Cause, are God,
and You turned their hearts backwards.” (I Kings 18:36–37)
And fire of the Cause came down
and consumed the offering and the wood
and the stones and the ash,
and licked up the water that was in the trench,
And all the people saw this
and fell on their faces
and said, “The Cause, They are the God!
The Cause, They are the God!” (I Kings 18:38–39)

tei:l.tei:note: And they blast:

tei:lg.tei:l: t’qiah, sh’varim, t’qiah.

tei:l.tei:note: and after that say:

tei:lg.tei:l: May the One who answered Elijah at Mt. Carmel
answer us and hear the sound of our prayers on this day,
for a Deity who hears prayers are You.
Blessed are You, Cause, who hears shouts.
And respond: Amen.
From the depths I have called You, Cause.
Master, hear my voice,
may Your ears be inclined to the sound of my petitions!
If You account for iniquities, Yah, Master,
who can stand?
For with You is forgiveness,
that You be revered.
I wait for the Cause,
my being awaits,
for Their word I have hoped.
My being is for the Master
as those watching for the morning
watch for the morning.
Israel, hope for the Cause,
for with the Cause is mercy and great redemption.
And They will redeem Israel from all its iniquities. (Psalms 130:1-8)
Answer us, Cause, answer us,
and at this time and at this season!
And as You answered Jonah in the gut of the fish
answer us, as it is written:
And Jonah prayed to the Cause
from the gut of the fish.
And he said, “I have called from my stress to the Cause, who answered me;
from the stomach of the underworld I have cried out,
You heard my voice.
But You threw me to the abyss, in the heart of the seas,
and the currents surrounded me,
all Your breakers and waves oper me passed.
And I had been saying to myself,
‘I am driven away from before Your eyes,
lo, would I again gaze upon Your holy Palace?’
Waters encompassed me to the neck,
the depths surrounded me,
the seaweed knotted over my head.
To the mountains’ bases I sunk,
the earth’s bars over me forever —
but You brought my life from the Pit, Cause my God.
As my soul was turning away, the Cause I remembered,
and my prayer came to You, to Your holy Palace.
Those keeping fallacious lies abandon their mercy.
But as for me, with a sound of thanksgiving I should offer to You,
let me fulfill what I vowed!
Salvation is the Cause’s!” (Jonah 2:2–10)
And the Cause talked to the fish,
and it vomited up Jonah onto dry land. (Jonah 2:11)

tei:l.tei:note: And they blast:

tei:lg.tei:l: t’qiah, t’ruah, t’qiah.

tei:l.tei:note: and after that say:

tei:lg.tei:l: May the One who answered Jonah in the gut of the fish
answer us at this time of our stress on this day,
for a Deity who answers at a time of stress are You.
Blessed are You, Cause, who answers at a time of stress.
And respond: Amen.
A prayer of the poor one who is faint,
and before the Cause pours out his plea.
Cause, hear my prayer,
that my cry should come before You!
Do not hide Your face from me
on the day of my stress,
turn Your ear to me on the day I call,
quickly answer me! (Psalms 102:1-3)
For gone like smoke are my days,
and my bones are scorched like a hearth;
struck and withered like grass is my heart,
forgetting to eat my food;
from the sound of my groaning
my bones stick to my skin.
I am like the desert owl,
the little-owl in the ruins.
Insomniac, I am like a bird alone on a roof. (Psalms 102:4-8)
All day my enemies abuse me,
boasters swear at me.
For ash like bread I have eaten,
and my drink I mixed with tears,
from Your rage and anger,
as You took me and cast me off.
My days like a long shadow,
I dry up like grass.
But You, Cause, are forever enthroned,
and Your memory is from age to age. (Psalms 102:9-13)
You will rise, have compassion on Ẓíōn,
for it is time to grace her, for the time has come!
For Your servants desire its stones
and love its dust.
And the nations will revere the Cause’s name,
and all the earth’s kings Your glory.
For the Cause built Ẓíōn,
appearing in Their glory.
They have turned to the prayer of the stripped-bare,
and have not ignored their prayer. (Psalms 102:14-18)
Let this be written for a later age,
that a people to be created may praise Yah.
For They gaze down from Their holy heights,
from heaven to earth They look,
to hear the groan of the bound,
to release those doomed to death,
to tell in Ẓíōn the name of the Cause,
and Their praise in Jerusalem,
when the peoples are gathered together,
and the kingdoms to serve the Cause. (Psalms 102:19-23)
They afflicted my strength on the way, shortened my days.
I say, “My Deity, do not take me out halfway through my days,
You whose years are ages upon ages!”
Of old You founded the earth,
Your handiwork is heaven.
They will perish,
but You, You will remain,
but everything will wear out like a garment,
like clothing You will replace them
and they will be replaced.
But You and Your years will not cease.
May Your servants’ children abide,
and their seed endure before You. (Psalms 102:24-29)
Our God and God of our ancestors,
have compassion on us per Your great compassion,
and just as You answered David and Solomon his son
answer us, as written:
And all Aravnah gave the king, to the king,
and Aravnah said to the king,
“The Cause your God desires you.”
And the king said to Aravnah,
“No, I will buy, buy it from you at price,
that I not offer up to the Cause my God worthless offerings!”
And David bought the threshing-floor and the cattle
for fifty shekels of silver.
And David there built an altar to the Cause
and offered up whole-offerings and peace-offerings,
and the Cause heeded the land
and the plague was stopped from upon Israel. (II Samuel 24:23–25)
And it says:
When Your people goes out to war on its foe
on the path that You send them,
and prays to the Cause towards the city that You chose
and the house that I built in Your name,
You will hear [in] heaven their prayers and petitions,
and do justice for them.
And if they sin against You —
for there is no person who does not sin! —
and You are enraged at them and give them over to the enemy,
and their exiles are exiled to the land of the enemy,
whether far or near,
and they turn their heart to the land from where they were exiled,
they will return and plead to You in the land of their exile, quote:
“We sinned, and we did iniquity, we were evil,”
and return to you with all their hearts
and with all their souls. (I Kings 8:44–48)

tei:l.tei:note: And they blast:

tei:lg.tei:l: t’qiah, sh’varim, t’ruah, t’qiah,
t’qiah, sh’varim, t’qiah,
t’qiah, t’ruah, t’qiah

tei:l.tei:note: and after that say:

tei:lg.tei:l: May the One who answered David and Solomon his son in Jerusalem
answer us and hear the sound of our shouts on this day,
for a Deity who hears shouts are You.
Blessed are You, Cause, who has compassion on the land.
And respond: Amen.

tei:l.tei:note: And return to their prayer and say:

tei:lg.tei:l: Heal us, Cause, that we be healed,
save us that we be saved,
for our praise are You,
and bring complete healing
to all our plagues and to all our sicknesses,
for a Deity healing, compassionate, and faithful etc.

tei:note.tei:p: Probably intended to be “the rabbis of blessed memory” but the zayin is missing from the abbreviation

The conclusion of the sixth blessing, also known as birkat seliḥah. Seliḥot piyyuṭim were originally inserted into this blessing, and in western Ashkenazi rites on fast days it still is. This is the origin of the name!
The conclusion of the seventh blessing. The ‘Aqedah passage is inserted into the seventh blessing instead of having its own blessing.

This first line, also found at the end of the blessing, is recorded in a later distinctive hand (sloppy, cursive, and unvocalized). Perhaps it was recited by the community before the prayer leader continues with the ‘Aqedah. The community reciting the Mi she-Anah passages prior to the prayer leader is found in other maḥzorim.
The seventh and eighth blessings of a weekday ‘amidah. Find B. Taanit 13b
A note to skip the Rosh Hashanah specific lines in the Zikhronot blessing.
Not found in the regular shofrot verses!
The opening of the eighth blessing of the ‘amidah on regular weekdays.
